os_sart_reconstruct — TOMOGRAPHY ct_scan op

• Data kinds: projstack × ctgeometry → voxel

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.os_sart_reconstruct(projections, geometry, n_iter=10, n_subsets=16, relaxation=0.8, initial=None, nonnegative=True, device='auto', on_iter=None) (to call the implementation directly, import ctscan; ctscan.os_sart_reconstruct(projections, geometry, n_iter=10, n_subsets=16, relaxation=0.8, initial=None, nonnegative=True, device='auto', on_iter=None); from the registry, opstomography.get("os_sart_reconstruct"))

• GPU: none (CPU reference implementation only)

Usage

OS-SART: the SIRT update applied to one ordered subset of views at a time.

One iteration passes over all subsets, so it costs about one SIRT iteration and moves about *n_subsets* times as far early on. With inconsistent data it settles into a limit cycle rather than a point.

:param projections: (view, V, U) line integrals. :param geometry: dict from ct_scan_geometry. :param n_iter: passes over all subsets, 1 .. 5000. :param n_subsets: subsets, 1 .. n_views. :param relaxation: step lam, (0, 2). :param initial: starting volume; None gives zeros. :param nonnegative: clip to >= 0 after each subset. :param device: "auto", "cpu" or "cuda". :param on_iter: optional on_iter(iteration, volume). :returns: (Z, Y, X) float volume. :raises ValueError: on a shape that disagrees with the geometry, a relaxation

outside (0, 2), or more subsets than views. Empty input (projections

with 0 elements) raises ValueError.
